projects.name: web-ocean
projects.title: Waves, sunsets and foam rendered live in one small web page
projects.summary: A WebGPU ocean renderer with no Three.js or game engine: WGSL compute shaders simulate multi-scale FFT waves, with sky, foam, reflections and a free camera.
projects.reason: Made public on October 16 at 16:49 Los Angeles time, with a self-contained HTML file and full shader source. A web graphics experiment you can see working immediately, useful for background scenes, visualization and AI-assisted graphics work. Recent star growth not verified.
projects.use_case: Understand WebGPU compute and render pipelines quickly, or explore immersive web backgrounds and interactive visuals with one complete small scene.
projects.requirements: A recent Chrome with WebGPU and a usable GPU; the official self-contained ocean.html opens directly. The development source needs Node.js, with esbuild used only for builds. No model, account or paid API.
projects.assessment: The pinned official engine ran in a local browser: all three sea states, sun height, dragging and pause work. A quick way to see what WebGPU can do visually. The small scene runs at 800×450 and at most 30 fps, which does not represent every device.
projects.caution: The author says it was written with AI help, but the runtime is a deterministic graphics program that calls no AI. Open sea only, with no shoreline or objects; clouds are a flat layer. Visuals and performance need testing on your own machine; upstream screenshots are no substitute.

projects.name: leanrea
projects.title: A short skill that has agents call local reverse-engineering tools directly
projects.summary: Built around a Markdown skill that picks a local CLI path per target (Electron, native binaries, Go, APK, WASM), with an investigation order and rules for stating evidence.
projects.reason: Made public on October 16 at 19:53 Los Angeles time as a direct answer to REA, picked earlier: for small analyses existing CLIs already cover, it lets you compare whether "short skill + native tools" works better. The author's performance comparison has not been reproduced independently.
projects.use_case: Analyse build artifacts of software you own or are authorized to inspect: extract dependency versions, trace Electron IPC, or locate a small piece of native logic, choosing existing tools per target.
projects.requirements: The skill runs no MCP server, but still needs an agent that can run shell commands and the matching tools, such as Node/asar, Xcode command line tools, Go or JADX/Ghidra. Model calls come from whatever agent you use, so it is not "model-free"; tool coverage differs by platform.
projects.assessment: Keep an eye on it; good for a small side-by-side against an existing REA workflow. The skill, license and the author's benchmark method were checked; the skill was not installed and no target software was analysed, so this is no evidence that it fully replaces REA.
projects.caution: The author's "38% faster, 35% cheaper" comes from a small sample: one model, one machine, 4 tasks run 3 times each. In that table leanrea scores 74/75 and REA 75/75, so accuracy is not equal on every task, and the declared tool size is not the per-turn footprint. The skill's commands extract and write files; review them for your environment before use.

projects.name: Handwired
projects.title: Build runnable numeric networks in JavaScript, turning branches and state into circuits
projects.summary: A JavaScript builder organizes arithmetic, comparison, selection and state into FP32 numeric circuits, executed by the official CPU runtime; some JSON search examples use WebGPU.
projects.reason: Made public on October 14 at 19:15 Los Angeles time, with a Circuit builder, compiler, interpreter and interactive examples. It shows a new experimental direction, program logic as a differentiable numeric network; it does not convert arbitrary existing JavaScript.
projects.use_case: Understand how numeric circuits encode comparisons, branches and state; try differentiable programs and small interactions, not a replacement for business JavaScript or a way to train large models.
projects.requirements: The official project uses Bun (docs test 1.4.3). The CPU path needs no model, account or GPU; the GPU JSON search example needs a browser with WebGPU.
projects.assessment: Worth trying the smallest CPU branch experiment first to see whether circuit execution matches the reference JavaScript. A research project; the author's precision and performance claims do not generalize to every program.
projects.caution: The official docs say there is no tool that converts existing JS into a network; you write the builder. Execution is bound by FP32 precision, declared value ranges and fixed workloads. WebGPU performance, training and production readiness were not verified.

projects.name: Hy Memory / MemHub

projects.summary: The Hy Memory Python SDK handles chat, work and coding memory separately; MemHub in the same repository adds a local runtime, CLI and desktop manager so several AI apps, each authorized separately, can reuse memory.
projects.reason: Made public on October 15 Los Angeles time; MemHub v1.0.2 shipped on October 16 at 11:49, with the SDK at 2.0.2. It tries to keep both task experience and code version history, close to what long-running multi-agent coding needs.
projects.use_case: Reuse confirmed engineering experience across coding agents, or look up earlier implementation changes by repository and branch. Test fact conflicts, deletion and source isolation with a small synthetic sample first.
projects.requirements: The SDK needs Python >=3.9 and usually a compatible embedding endpoint; extraction in pro/ultra needs an LLM configured too. MemHub has its own runtime and optional built-in embeddings; development needs Python 3.12, Node.js 24, pnpm 11 and uv. Supported platforms follow the release manifest; Windows is not supported yet.
projects.assessment: Watch the memory layering, version history chains and per-app authorization closely. Only code, dependencies and release records were checked; no real conversations, storage or deletion tests, or recall quality checks were run.
projects.caution: "Production-grade" and the paper and benchmark results are the authors' claims, not verified locally. Local first does not mean every mode is fully offline; check the data flow when configuring an external LLM or embeddings. SDK and MemHub are different layers; the desktop requirements are not the SDK's minimum.

projects.title: Turn chat answers into charts, maps, calculators and interactive pages
projects.summary: A chat interface template driven by CopilotKit and AG-UI, combining a Next.js front end, a Python agent and generative UI rendered in iframes.
projects.reason: Announced by the CopilotKit team on October 9; close to UI and web development. Recent star growth not verified.
projects.use_case: Add interactive answers to an AI product, or study how front end, agent back end and isolated rendering fit together.
projects.requirements: Node 22+, pnpm 9+, Python 3.12+ and uv; the default setup needs two API keys, OpenAI and TypeSafe/Jev, billed to your own provider accounts.
projects.assessment: Worth trying the example and reading the implementation before deciding whether to integrate it into your product.
projects.caution: Not installed or tested yet. The demo video includes pre-rendered scenes and real output varies; for now it is best as an implementation reference.

tech_stack.note: These are the technologies the project is built with; OpenAI and Jev are the default model service settings and still need their keys.

projects.name: RDST
projects.title: Monitor slow PostgreSQL and MySQL queries and get tuning suggestions
projects.summary: A local database diagnostics tool and agent that reads execution plans to suggest indexes, configuration and SQL rewrites, with an MCP interface.
projects.reason: Shown on Show HN on October 15; at collection (13:01) the post was about an hour old with 5 points. An early find with little attention so far.
projects.use_case: Track down database performance problems after a web project goes live.
projects.requirements: Installers for macOS, Windows and Linux; needs a read-only database connection and query statistics. Automatic AI monitoring needs a Readyset login. Building from source needs Node 22+, pnpm 11, Python 3.10+ and uv.
projects.assessment: A concrete use case; keep an eye on real tuning results and user feedback.
projects.caution: Not installed or tested yet. AI analysis sends SQL, execution plans and table schemas; monitoring records stay on your machine. Do not treat its suggestions as verified performance gains.

heat.label: 5 points on Show HN
heat.window: Collected October 15 at 13:01, about an hour after posting

tech_stack.note: PostgreSQL / MySQL are the databases being diagnosed, not part of the project's interface or service framework.

projects.name: Endo
projects.title: Switch coding agents in one chat and orchestrate them with TypeScript
projects.summary: An Electron desktop app and local service that connect the Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity CLIs, with sessions, branching discussions, workflows and scheduled runs.
projects.reason: New on Show HN on October 15; v0.1.1 shipped on October 14 at 21:51 Los Angeles time with a signed Mac build and background updates. Little attention so far: an early find.
projects.use_case: If you already use several coding agents and want to keep context in one interface, or try repeatable multi-model drafting, review and debate workflows.
projects.requirements: The ready-made installer targets Apple Silicon Macs; sign in to at least one supported model provider. Development needs Node 24, Bun 1.4.2 and Just. The dev build installs pinned versions of the related CLIs on first launch; usage is still bound by each provider's account limits.
projects.assessment: Keep an eye on it. Bringing existing CLIs into one interface and orchestrating workflows is interesting, but it is 0.1.x; validate context hand-off, permissions and stability on small tasks first.
projects.caution: Only code, docs, license and releases were checked; not installed or tested. Full cross-provider history hand-off and workflow results are the author's claims, and the docs warn of breaking changes ahead. Running models in parallel uses each provider's quota.

heat.label: 4 points on Show HN
heat.window: Collected October 15 at 19:59, about 5 hours after posting; little attention, not a verified trend

tech_stack.note: The underlying coding agents connect through each provider's CLI; this is Endo's own core implementation.
